label: Men's ODI · 2nd innings
methodology: 100 most recent eligible completed second innings in the downloaded international archive. Separate cohort from first innings. Full-length six-ball-over fixtures only; DLS/reduced, incomplete, no-result and super-over matches excluded. Early all-outs and successful short chases retained through an innings-start checkpoint; later checkpoints only while active. Actual targets are known from the completed first innings. Final runs and wickets are measured at chase termination, not a hypothetical full innings. Winning boundary overshoots are retained. The unchanged model caps its run forecast at the target but does not fully model wickets until chase termination; interpret wicket errors accordingly. No future batting order supplied; at innings start openers are unknown. Current player/venue priors and learned adjustments may contain historical information. This is a retrospective replay, not leakage-free holdout validation or a test of live scraping.
summary: Across 460 predictions the model has an MAE of 22.0 runs and RMSE of 36.7 runs. Bias is +3.3 runs (the model overshoots on average). Final-wicket MAE is 3.32 wickets, with a signed bias of -3.13 wickets (predicted minus actual). Exact final-wicket counts occur in 13.0% of checkpoint predictions. The predicted range captures the actual score 74.3% of the time with an average range width of 63 runs. Error by final score bucket: low-scoring (<160): 22.1 runs MAE, mid-range (160–200): 23.4 runs MAE, high-scoring (200+): 21.4 runs MAE. Predictions are least accurate at the 0-over checkpoint (MAE 29.1 runs) and most accurate at 40 overs (MAE 14.4 runs).
